title: Systems of Linear Equations
seo_title: Algebra I Systems of Linear Equations Worksheets (TEKS A.5C)
standard_text: A.5C solve systems of two linear equations with two variables for mathematical and real-world problems; A.2I write systems of two linear equations given a table of values, a graph, and a verbal description; A.3F graph systems of two linear equations in two variables on the coordinate plane and determine the solutions if they exist; A.3G estimate graphically the solutions to systems of two linear equations with two variables in real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Algebra I systems worksheets for Texas TEKS A.5C, A.2I, A.3F and A.3G: solve by graphing, elimination and substitution, count solutions and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The solution is where the lines cross.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The solution of a system is the point where the lines cross.
  • Substitution: solve one equation for a variable and put it into the other.
  • Elimination: add or subtract the equations so one variable cancels. Multiply first if needed.
  • Parallel lines: no solution. The same line: infinitely many solutions.

Examples

Example

x + y = 10 and x − y = 4

add: 2x = 14

x = 7, y = 3

Answer: (7, 3)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Giving only one valueA solution is an ordered pair.
Not lining up termsLine up x, y and numbers.
Multiplying only one sideMultiply every term.

items.q: The graph shows y = x + 1 and y = −x + 5. What is the solution of the system?
items.e: The solution is where the lines cross: (2, 3). Check: 3 = 1 × 2 + 1 and 3 = −1 × 2 + 5.

items.q:

y = −x + 5?
c: No, it makes neither equation true
Yes, any point is a solution
Yes, it makes both equations true
No, it makes only one equation true
items.e: Put x = 2 in both: 3 and 3. Both give y = 3, so yes.

sets.title: One, none or infinitely many solutions

items.q:
How many solutions does y = 2x + 3
y = 2x − 1 have?
items.e: Same slope (2) but different y-intercepts (3 and −1): the lines are parallel and never meet. No solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = x + 4
y = −x + 4 have?
items.e: The slopes are different (1 and −1), so the lines cross once: one solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = 3x − 2
y = 3x − 2 have?
items.e: Same slope and same y-intercept: it is the same line. Infinitely many solutions.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = 12x + 1
y = 12x + 5 have?
items.e: Same slope (12) but different y-intercepts (1 and 5): the lines are parallel and never meet. No solution.

items.q: The first equation is y = 3x + 2. Which second equation gives no solution?
items.e: Use the same slope with a different y-intercept: parallel lines. The answer is y = 3x + 7.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = −2x + 5
y = 4x + 5 have?
items.e: The slopes are different (−2 and 4), so the lines cross once: one solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = −3x + 1
y = −3x + 1 have?
items.e: Same slope and same y-intercept: it is the same line. Infinitely many solutions.

items.q: The first equation is y = −2x + 1. Which second equation gives infinitely many solutions?
items.e: Divide by 2: y = −2x + 1. It is the same line. The answer is 2y = −4x + 2.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = 4x
y = 4x + 7 have?
items.e: Same slope (4) but different y-intercepts (0 and 7): the lines are parallel and never meet. No solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does y = 23x − 1
y = −1 12x + 2 have?
items.e: The slopes are different (23 and −1 12), so the lines cross once: one solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does 2x + y = 5
4x + 2y = 10 have?
items.e: The second equation is the first one times 2. Same line: infinitely many solutions.

items.q:
How many solutions does x + y = 3
x + y = 7 have?
items.e: x + y cannot be 3 and 7 at the same time. Parallel lines: no solution.

items.q: The first equation is y = 12x − 4. Which second equation gives one solution?
items.e: A different slope makes the lines cross once. The answer is y = −12x − 4.

items.q:
How many solutions does 3x − y = 2
x + y = 6 have?
items.e: y = 3x − 2 and y = −x + 6 have different slopes: one solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does 2x − 2y = 4
x − y = 2 have?
items.e: Divide the first by 2: x − y = 2. It is the second equation: infinitely many solutions.

items.q:
How many solutions does 4x + 2y = 8
2x + y = 3 have?
items.e: Divide the first by 2: 2x + y = 4, but the second says 2x + y = 3: no solution.

items.q: The first equation is y = 4x − 3. Which second equation gives no solution?
items.e: Use the same slope with a different y-intercept: parallel lines. The answer is y = 4x + 2.

items.q:
How many solutions does x − 2y = 4
2x + y = 3 have?
items.e: y = ½x − 2 and y = −2x + 3 have different slopes: one solution.

items.q:
How many solutions does −3x + 3y = 9
x − y = −3 have?
items.e: Divide the first by −3: x − y = −3, the same as the second: infinitely many solutions.

items.q:
How many solutions does 5x + 5y = 10
x + y = 1 have?
items.e: Divide the first by 5: x + y = 2, but the second says x + y = 1: no solution.

items.q: A phone plan charges a monthly fee plus a cost per GB. 3 GB costs $41 and 7 GB costs $61. What is the monthly fee?
items.e: 4 more GB cost $20, so 1 GB costs $5. Fee = 41 − 15 = $26.

items.q: A school play sold 300 tickets. Adult tickets cost $12 and student tickets cost $7. Ticket sales were $2,850. How many adult tickets were sold?
items.e: a + s = 300 and 12a + 7s = 2,850. Multiply the first by 7: 7a + 7s = 2,100. Subtract: 5a = 750, so a = 150.

items.q: Gym A charges $50 to join and $30 a month. Gym B charges $20 to join and $35 a month. After how many months do they cost the same?
How many solutions does the system y = 3x + 2 and y = 3x − 5 have?
items.e: Same slope, different intercepts: the lines are parallel, so there is no solution.

items.q: Ethan solves a system and gets x = 2, y = 5. How can he check?
items.e: The pair must make both equations true.

items.q: A rectangle's perimeter is 54 ft. Its length is 3 ft less than twice its width. What is its length?
At a fair, 3 hot dogs and 2 lemonades cost $16. 2 hot dogs and 4 lemonades cost $16. How much is a lemonade?
items.e: Multiply the first by 2: 6h + 4l = 32. Subtract the second: 4h = 16, so h = 4 and l = $2.

items.q: A boat goes 36 miles downstream in 2 hours and 36 miles back upstream in 3 hours. What is the speed of the current?
items.e: b + c = 18 and b − c = 12. Subtract: 2c = 6, so c = 3 mph (and the boat goes 15 mph).

items.q: 2 burgers and 3 drinks cost $18.50. 4 burgers and 1 drink cost $24.50. How much is one burger?
items.e: Double the first: 4b + 6d = 37. Subtract the second: 5d = 12.50, so d = 2.50 and b = $5.50.

items.q: A chemist mixes a 10% acid solution with a 40% acid solution to make 30 L of a 20% solution. How many liters of the 10% solution are used?
items.e: a + b = 30 and 0.1a + 0.4b = 6. Multiply the first by 0.1 and subtract: 0.3b = 3, so b = 10 and a = 20 L.

items.q: Two numbers add up to 20. Their difference is 6. What are the numbers?
items.e: x + y = 20 and x − y = 6. Add: 2x = 26, so x = 13 and y = 7. The answer is 13 and 7.

items.q: Adult tickets cost $8 and child tickets cost $5. 10 tickets cost $62. How many adult tickets were sold?
A farm has chickens and cows: 15 heads and 44 legs. How many cows are there?
Gym A: $20 to join and $15 a month. Gym B: $50 to join and $10 a month. After how many months is the total cost the same?
items.e: 20 + 15m = 50 + 10m, so 5m = 30 and m = 6 months.

items.q: Pens cost $2 and notebooks cost $3. Kim buys 9 items for $22. How many notebooks does she buy?
A boat goes 24 miles downstream in 2 hours and back upstream in 3 hours. What is the speed of the boat in still water?
items.e: b + c = 12 and b − c = 8. Add: 2b = 20, so b = 10 mph (current 2 mph).

items.q: The sum of two numbers is 35. One number is 4 times the other. What is the larger number?
items.e: x + y = 35 and y = 4x. Then 5x = 35, x = 7 and y = 28.

items.q: Hot dogs cost $3 and drinks cost $2. Sam buys 2 hot dogs and 3 drinks. Lee buys 4 hot dogs and 1 drink. Who pays more?
A rectangle's perimeter is 30 cm. Its length is 3 cm more than its width. What is the width?
Mia has 14 coins, all dimes and quarters. They are worth $2.30. How many quarters does she have?
